summary: @servicetitan/anvil2-ext-common preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package advertises itself as a React UI component library but declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style identifier mangling and string-array indirection) and, when run by npm install, downloads the Bun runtime zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, unpacks the bun binary, and invokes it via execFileSync against a bundled sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB file starting with '// @bun @bun-cjs' and heavily obfuscated with string-array rotation and hex-mangled identifiers, concealing its actual behavior. Fetching an alternate JavaScript runtime at preinstall specifically to execute an obfuscated in-tree blob is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: the payload does not run under Node so Node-based scanners and lifecycle hooks in the consuming project's toolchain do not observe it, and its contents cannot be inspected without deobfuscation. A UI component library has no legitimate reason to fetch a runtime and execute an unreadable 727KB payload at install time, and the name 'math_init.js' does not correspond to any advertised functionality of the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
